items.note: RCT in a three-day hackathon: 22 early-career social scientists randomized to unrestricted GPT-4 or no AI; experts scored manuscripts on six dimensions including originality (AI raised clarity and coherence only). Abstract read from the Research Square version (10.21203/rs.3.rs-6937665/v2); same study as the SSRN record; below the 50-participant threshold.

Controlled experiment comparing a divergent or convergent LLM persona with a standard answer-giving LLM on a creative problem-solving task, with objective creativity measures; AI-vs-AI comparison only (no no-AI arm per search notes, which report 105 recruited and 101 analyzed); the abstract states no N or random assignment.

Three-paper doctoral thesis; paper 2 reports three experiments comparing GenAI-assisted and human-only consumer product ideation, with novelty and appropriateness outcomes; full text embargoed, N not stated, and the experiments likely overlap with Sabbah, Banerjee, Li (c542).

Experiment with 400 professionals in four ideation configurations (human-only, unstructured GenAI collaboration, GenAI seeding, TC-based GenAI seeding), with expert ratings of novelty, utility, feasibility; AOM Proceedings version (10.5465/amproc.2026.48bp) reports n = 350 and adds semantic-similarity analyses; likely overlaps with the Sabbah thesis (c541).

Within-subject study with 20 programmers, LLM-assisted vs unassisted, measuring idea-generation time, creative moments, and the number of ideas in solutions; order randomization not stated; below the 50-participant threshold.

Preregistered within-subject experiment: Japanese and American participants wrote workplace emails without AI, with a low-context AI draft, and with a high-context AI draft; outcome is cultural style markers (convergence toward the draft), so whether it counts as a creativity or diversity outcome needs full-text review; search notes report 175 participants and counterbalanced order, not in the abstract.

50 education-technology students randomly assigned to learning with GAI tools or traditional instruction, with a post-test on an 18-item creativity scale (fluency, flexibility, originality, elaboration); the abstract also calls it quasi-experimental, and the scale may be self-report rather than a scored task; check whether AI was available at the post-test.

Indonesian quasi-experiment with 70 grade-10 students in two classes (35 Gemini-assisted math instruction, 35 control), with a creative-thinking test (N-gain 0.617 vs 0.504) and an adversity-quotient questionnaire; class-level, non-random assignment.

Pilot study in which 30 novice designers generated ideas with traditional methods and with an LLM conversational ideation interface; an expert panel compared fluency, novelty, and variety qualitatively; mainly a tool paper; journal version of arXiv 2409.05747; below the 50-participant threshold.

Five-week quasi-experiment with 186 undergraduates (87 using ChatGPT and Midjourney in digital storytelling vs 99 control), randomized at the department level; outcomes are design-thinking mindset, creative self-efficacy, and reflective-thinking self-efficacy, all self-reported.
